sections.title: Getting started
sections.body:
Install the APK on phone A (the controller). Direct USB is the main connection mode; wireless is optional. B does not need another APK: the client copies and starts the official scrcpy 3.3.4 server through ADB.
A requires Android 8+. B requires Android 5+ for video, Android 11+ for output audio, and Android 12+ for camera capture. Compatibility with future Android updates depends on the server version.

sections.title: Direct USB
sections.body:
1. On B, enable Developer options → USB debugging. Wireless debugging is not needed for this mode.
2. Connect A and B with a DATA cable. A must be the USB host/OTG device (the phone controlling USB); B is the USB device. Some models require enabling OTG or changing “USB controlled by”. An OTG adapter on A can help establish the roles.
3. Open Scrcpy on A and allow USB access. The app does not open itself when the cable is connected.
4. Unlock B, accept “Allow USB debugging”, and select “Always allow” for A’s key if you want to keep the authorization.
5. Automatic USB connection only starts a new session while Scrcpy is in the foreground. Open the app yourself after connecting the cable, or tap Connect USB manually. If several ADB devices are connected, choose B from the list.
After authorization, no IP address, ports, wireless codes or PC are needed. Some Android versions ask for USB access on A again when the cable is reconnected; this is a system dialog.
Unplugging the cable closes the session and releases USB resources. Reconnecting the cable triggers another connection attempt only while the app is in the foreground and automatic connection is enabled. A manually disconnected session stays stopped until you tap Connect USB or reconnect the cable.
Video, audio and control use the same scrcpy channels, including direct multitouch with separate finger IDs, trackpad mouse control, clipboard and recording. Direct USB here is not scrcpy’s --otg/HID mode, which controls the device without video mirroring.

sections.title: USB troubleshooting
sections.body:
• B is missing: check that the cable supports data, A is the host/OTG device, and USB debugging is enabled on B. Reconnect the cable after enabling debugging.
• A detects B but video does not start: check B for the “Allow USB debugging” prompt, then open the session console for ADB/server messages.
• On Xiaomi, if video works but touch does not, check “USB debugging (Security settings)” on B.
• Cannot switch roles: check USB settings on both phones, or connect an OTG adapter to A and use a data cable to B.
• Stuttering: try the balanced 1280 / 60 FPS / 8 Mbps profile or a lower resolution. USB speed and power depend on the hardware and cable.

sections.title: Wireless pairing
sections.body:
1. On B, enable Developer options → Wireless debugging.
2. Open “Pair device with pairing code”. On A, enter B’s IP address, PAIRING port and 6-digit code, then tap Pair A with B.
3. Close the pairing-code window on B. Use the CONNECTION IP:port from the main Wireless debugging page on A, then tap Connect over network.
The pairing port and connection port are different. Android may change the connection port after disabling debugging or changing networks. Update it when needed.

sections.title: Classic ADB TCP
sections.body:
On a PC with B connected and authorized over USB:

Then enter B’s IP and port 5555 on A. Accept A’s key on B when prompted. On some Xiaomi devices, “USB debugging (Security settings)” is also required for input control.

topics.title: Controls and zoom
topics.summary: Touch, mouse buttons and local zoom

sections.title: Interaction
sections.body: Your mode is remembered for later sessions. Switching mode releases any active mouse buttons and touch points.

sections.title: Direct touch
sections.body: touch the desired point on the image. Each finger’s ID, coordinates and pressure are sent separately. Pinch and other multitouch gestures in this mode are sent to B rather than converted into mouse clicks. The number of simultaneous fingers depends on A and B.

sections.title: Gesture touchpad
sections.body: move a finger to move the cursor; tap briefly to click; hold a finger still, then move it to drag. At 1×, move two fingers together to scroll. This is relative input, similar to a VNC viewer.

sections.title: Touchpad with buttons
sections.body: move a finger over the image to move the cursor. Clicks are sent only through Left and Right, overlaid across the full width near the bottom of the image. The buttons have transparent interiors and visible outlines, including while pressed. Hold Left with one finger and move another finger over the image to drag. Lifting the finger from the trackpad area does not release a button you are still holding. At 1×, moving two fingers together over the image scrolls B.

sections.title: Local zoom in both Touchpad modes
sections.body: pinch on the image to zoom between 1× and 6×. Video is enlarged and cropped only on A; no pinch gesture, zoom command or resolution change is sent to B. When zoomed, move two fingers together to pan the crop. At 1×, parallel two-finger movement scrolls B. Lift all fingers before starting a new gesture after a pinch. Mouse buttons are independent of gestures on the image. The ••• menu has Zoom −, Reset 1× and Zoom +. Direct touch resets local zoom to 1× and preserves remote multitouch.

The small ••• button opens the session menu; drag it to reposition it. The menu provides control modes, Actions and tools, Console and commands, and Disconnect session. The main menu and Actions page stay open after an action. Close explicitly with ×, Back to control or Back on A; tapping outside does not close the menu. Actions include navigation, volume/mute, screen power, Android panels, clipboard, screenshots and diagnostics. You can press Volume + / − repeatedly without reopening the menu. Text-entry dialogs and Console open above the menu and return to it when closed.
Back on A opens the session menu. Use the remote Back action to press Back on B.
Physical keyboard keycodes are forwarded while viewing the session. For Unicode text, use Send text / Clipboard.

sections.title: App language
sections.body: At the very bottom of Settings, open Language and choose English or Română. The interface and this guide update immediately; your choice is saved. Video settings, connection details and the ADB key are kept. The app’s name is Scrcpy in both languages.

sections.title: USB quality profile
sections.body: 1920 px, 60 FPS, 24000000 bits/s (24 Mbps), h264. Like other video settings, it applies to the next connection.

sections.title: Each editable setting has a ▾ button with concrete values and Enter manually…; you can still type a value. Resolutions
sections.body: original / 4320 / 3840 / 2560 / 2400 / 2160 / 1920 / 1600 / 1440 / 1280 / 1024 / 960 / 800 / 720 / 640 / 480 px. FPS: unlimited / 24 / 25 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 90 / 120 / 144 / 165 / 180 / 240. Video bitrate: 0.5 to 150 Mbps, with intermediate values. There are also choices for audio bitrate, camera FPS and size, orientation, angle, virtual display and cursor speed. These are requested settings; actual supported modes depend on the devices.

sections.title: Balanced profile
sections.body: resolution 1280, 60 FPS, bitrate 8000000, h264.

sections.title: Low bandwidth
sections.body: resolution 800, 30 FPS, bitrate 2000000; audio off if needed.

sections.title: Original resolution
sections.body: max_size=0. This increases bandwidth and decoding requirements.

sections.title: HEVC
sections.body: video_codec=h265. AV1: video_codec=av1. Both devices need compatible codecs. If video stays black, switch back to h264.

sections.title: Camera
sections.body: video_source=camera, camera_facing=back, camera_size=1920x1080. Screen input control is disabled automatically for camera sessions.

sections.title: Rotation
sections.body: capture_orientation=90. Lock orientation: capture_orientation=@0.

sections.title: Microphone audio
sections.body: audio=true and audio_source=mic. Output/playback capture depends on Android and the captured app’s policy.

sections.title: max_size
sections.body:
Maximum resolution • px.

Default: 1280. 0 = original size; 1280 is a good starting point.

Example value: 1280.

sections.title: video_bit_rate
sections.body:
Video bitrate • bits/s.

Default: 8000000. 8 Mbps = 8000000. Try 2000000 for a weak Wi-Fi connection.

Example value: 8000000.

sections.title: max_fps
sections.body:
Maximum FPS.

Default: 60. 30 / 60 / 90 / 120; the actual frame rate depends on B and the connection.

Example value: 60.

sections.title: video_codec
sections.body:
Video codec.

Default: h264. h264|h265|av1

Example value: h264.

sections.title: video_source

sections.title: display_id

Example value: 0.

sections.title: crop

sections.title: capture_orientation

sections.title: angle

Example value: 0.

Example value: (a name from Encoders).

sections.title: video_codec_options

Audio from B.

Audio codec.

Default: aac. aac|opus|raw|flac

sections.title: audio_bit_rate

Audio bitrate • bits/s.

Example value: 128000.

sections.title: audio_source

Audio source.

sections.title: audio_dup
sections.body:
Keep audio playing on B.

Audio encoder.

sections.title: audio_codec_options
sections.body:
Audio encoder options.

sections.title: camera_id
sections.body:
Camera ID.

Default: empty / automatic. Empty = automatic. Available for the camera source on Android 12+.

Example value: 0.

sections.title: camera_facing
sections.body:
Preferred camera.

Default: empty / automatic. |front|back|external

Example value: back.

sections.title: camera_size
sections.body:
Camera size.

Default: empty / automatic. Example: 1920x1080. Empty = automatic.

sections.title: camera_fps
sections.body:
Camera FPS.

Default: 30. 30 or 60, if supported.

Example value: 30.

sections.title: camera_high_speed
sections.body:
High speed camera.

Default: false. true/false switch.

Example value: false.

sections.title: new_display
sections.body:
Virtual display.

Default: empty / automatic. Empty = disabled; example: 1280x720/240. Depends on B’s Android version.

Example value: 1280x720/240.

sections.title: control
sections.body:
Allow control.

Default: true. true/false switch.

Example value: true.

sections.title: show_touches
sections.body:
Show touches on B.

Default: false. true/false switch.

Example value: false.

sections.title: stay_awake
sections.body:
Keep B awake while charging.

Default: false. true/false switch.

Example value: false.

sections.title: power_off_on_close
sections.body:
Turn off B’s screen on exit.

Default: false. true/false switch.

Example value: false.

sections.body:
Receive clipboard from B.

sections.title: downsize_on_error
sections.body:
Reduce resolution on error.

sections.title: screenOff
sections.body:
Turn off B’s screen on connect.

Default: false. true/false switch.

Example value: false.

sections.title: reconnect
sections.body:
Reconnect automatically.

Default: true. true/false switch.

Example value: true.

sections.title: mouseSpeed
sections.body:
Cursor speed.

Default: 1.2. 0.2–5.0; mouse mode is a relative trackpad with a local cursor.

Example value: 1.2.

sections.title: extra
sections.body:
Extra server options.

Default: empty / automatic. One key=value per line. Help contains the full catalog; these are not CLI --... arguments.

Example value: log_level=debug.

sections.title: Recording
sections.body: enable record, video_codec=h264, and audio_codec=aac if audio is enabled. MP4 is produced from the compressed stream and finalized on disconnect. A change to the video configuration, such as rotation, ends the current recording. Reconnecting starts a new file. Export last recording / screenshot copies it to a folder of your choice.

sections.title: Screenshots
sections.body: PNG screenshots save the image shown on A, at the size of the displayed surface.

sections.title: Export
sections.body: Open ••• → Actions and tools → Export last screenshot / recording. Choose a destination folder. The latest finished file is available after the session ends.

sections.title: record
sections.body:
Record MP4 on A.

Default: false. true/false switch.

Example value: false.

topics.title: Console and shell
topics.summary: Log levels and commands for phone B

sections.title: Reading the console
sections.body: INFO is neutral, OK is green, WARN is amber, ERROR is red, and CMD is blue. Each entry groups its metadata above the message. USB, ADB, VIDEO, AUDIO and other tags identify the source. Copy and Export keep plain text; colors are only used on screen.

sections.title: Console
sections.body:
Shows server commands, B’s stdout/stderr, shell-command output and client errors. Copy, Clear and Export act on the log. Clear empties both the log file and the visible console. Copy attempts to copy the complete log; use Export for large logs. The screen keeps the last 2 MB; the file contains everything since the last Clear.
During a session: ••• → Console and commands. Commands run in B’s ADB shell. This is not an interactive terminal emulator: each command starts a separate shell. Use Stop shell commands for long-running commands. Output from B and third-party libraries is shown verbatim, in its original language.

topics.title: Desktop reference
topics.summary: PC commands and the full scrcpy manual

sections.title: PC only
sections.body: The options in this section are for scrcpy on a PC. This Android client supports only the features described above. On a PC, scrcpy.exe --help gives the exact list for the installed version.

sections.body: HEVC compression, if supported by the phone and PC.

sections.body: record into the scrcpy folder.

sections.body: select a device (adb devices lists serials).

sections.body: connect over the network with ADB already enabled.

sections.title: NAME
sections.body: scrcpy - Display and control your Android device

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.body:
scrcpy
[ options ]

sections.title: DESCRIPTION
sections.body:
scrcpy
provides display and control of Android devices connected on USB (or over TCP/IP). It does not require any root access.

sections.title: --always-on-top
sections.body: Make scrcpy window always on top (above other windows).

sections.title: --angle  degrees
sections.body: Rotate the video content by a custom angle, in degrees (clockwise).

sections.title: --audio-bit-rate  value
sections.body:
Encode the audio at the given bit rate, expressed in bits/s. Unit suffixes are supported: 'K' (x1000) and 'M' (x1000000).

Default is 128K (128000).

sections.title: --audio-buffer  ms
sections.body:
Configure the audio buffering delay (in milliseconds).

Lower values decrease the latency, but increase the likelihood of buffer underrun (causing audio glitches).

Default is 50.

sections.title: --audio-codec  name
sections.body:
Select an audio codec (opus, aac, flac or raw).

Default is opus.

sections.title: --audio-codec-options  key[:type]=value[,...]
sections.body:
Set a list of comma-separated key:type=value options for the device audio encoder.

The possible values for 'type' are 'int' (default), 'long', 'float' and 'string'.

The list of possible codec options is available in the Android documentation:

<https://d.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaFormat>

sections.title: --audio-dup
sections.body:
Duplicate audio (capture and keep playing on the device).

This feature is only available with --audio-source=playback.

sections.title: --audio-encoder  name
sections.body:
Use a specific MediaCodec audio encoder (depending on the codec provided by --audio-codec).

The available encoders can be listed by --list-encoders.

sections.title: --audio-source  source
sections.body:
Select the audio source. Possible values are:

 - output: forwards the whole audio output, and disables playback on the device.
 - playback: captures the audio playback (Android apps can opt-out, so the whole output is not necessarily captured).
 - mic: captures the microphone.
 - mic-unprocessed: captures the microphone unprocessed (raw) sound.
 - mic-camcorder: captures the microphone tuned for video recording, with the same orientation as the camera if available.
 - mic-voice-recognition: captures the microphone tuned for voice recognition.
 - mic-voice-communication: captures the microphone tuned for voice communications (it will for instance take advantage of echo cancellation or automatic gain control if available).
 - voice-call: captures voice call.
 - voice-call-uplink: captures voice call uplink only.
 - voice-call-downlink: captures voice call downlink only.
 - voice-performance: captures audio meant to be processed for live performance (karaoke), includes both the microphone and the device playback.

Default is output.

sections.title: --audio-output-buffer  ms
sections.body:
Configure the size of the SDL audio output buffer (in milliseconds).

If you get robotic audio playback, you should test with a higher value (10). Do not change this setting otherwise.

Default is 5.

-b, --video-bit-rate  value
Encode the video at the given bit rate, expressed in bits/s. Unit suffixes are supported: 'K' (x1000) and 'M' (x1000000).

Default is 8M (8000000).

sections.title: --camera-ar  ar
sections.body:
Select the camera size by its aspect ratio (+/- 10%).

Possible values are sensor (use the camera sensor aspect ratio), num:den (e.g. 4:3) and value (e.g. 1.6).

sections.title: --camera-facing  facing
sections.body:
Select the device camera by its facing direction.

Possible values are front, back and external.

sections.title: --camera-fps  fps
sections.body:
Specify the camera capture frame rate.

If not specified, Android's default frame rate (30 fps) is used.

sections.title: --camera-high-speed
sections.body:
Enable high-speed camera capture mode.

This mode is restricted to specific resolutions and frame rates, listed by --list-camera-sizes.

sections.title: --camera-id  id
sections.body:
Specify the device camera id to mirror.

The available camera ids can be listed by --list-cameras.

sections.title: --camera-size  widthxheight
sections.body: Specify an explicit camera capture size.

sections.title: --capture-orientation  value
sections.body:
Possible values are 0, 90, 180, 270, flip0, flip90, flip180 and flip270, possibly prefixed by '@'.

The number represents the clockwise rotation in degrees; the flip keyword applies a horizontal flip before the rotation.

If a leading '@' is passed (@90) for display capture, then the rotation is locked, and is relative to the natural device orientation.

If '@' is passed alone, then the rotation is locked to the initial device orientation.

Default is 0.

sections.title: --crop  width:height:x:y
sections.body:
Crop the device screen on the server.

The values are expressed in the device natural orientation (typically, portrait for a phone, landscape for a tablet).

-d, --select-usb
Use USB device (if there is exactly one, like adb -d).

Also see -e (--select-tcpip).

sections.title: --disable-screensaver
sections.body: Disable screensaver while scrcpy is running.

sections.title: --display-id  id
sections.body:
Specify the device display id to mirror.

The available display ids can be listed by --list-displays.

Default is 0.

sections.title: --display-ime-policy  value
sections.body:
Set the policy for selecting where the IME should be displayed.

Possible values are local, fallback and hide:

 - local means that the IME should appear on the local display.
 - fallback means that the IME should appear on a fallback display (the default display).
 - hide means that the IME should be hidden.

By default, the IME policy is left unchanged.

sections.title: --display-orientation  value
sections.body:
Set the initial display orientation.

Possible values are 0, 90, 180, 270, flip0, flip90, flip180 and flip270. The number represents the clockwise rotation in degrees; the flip keyword applies a horizontal flip before the rotation.

Default is 0.

-e, --select-tcpip
Use TCP/IP device (if there is exactly one, like adb -e).

Also see -d (--select-usb).

-f, --fullscreen
Start in fullscreen.

sections.title: --force-adb-forward
sections.body:
Do not attempt to use adb reverse to connect to the device.

-G
Same as --gamepad=uhid, or --keyboard=aoa if --otg is set.

sections.title: --gamepad  mode
sections.body:
Select how to send gamepad inputs to the device.

Possible values are disabled, uhid and aoa:

 - disabled does not send gamepad inputs to the device.
 - uhid simulates physical HID gamepads using the Linux HID kernel module on the device.
 - aoa simulates physical HID gamepads using the AOAv2 protocol. It may only work over USB.

Also see --keyboard\f and R--mouse.
-h, --help
Print this help.

-K
Same as --keyboard=uhid, or --keyboard=aoa if --otg is set.

sections.title: --keyboard  mode
sections.body:
Select how to send keyboard inputs to the device.

Possible values are disabled, sdk, uhid and aoa:

 - disabled does not send keyboard inputs to the device.
 - sdk uses the Android system API to deliver keyboard events to applications.
 - uhid simulates a physical HID keyboard using the Linux HID kernel module on the device.
 - aoa simulates a physical HID keyboard using the AOAv2 protocol. It may only work over USB.

For uhid and aoa, the keyboard layout must be configured (once and for all) on the device, via Settings -> System -> Languages and input -> Physical keyboard. This settings page can be started directly using the shortcut MOD+k (except in OTG mode), or by executing:

    adb shell am start -a android.settings.HARD_KEYBOARD_SETTINGS

This option is only available when the HID keyboard is enabled (or a physical keyboard is connected).

Also see --mouse and --gamepad.

sections.title: --kill-adb-on-close
sections.body: Kill adb when scrcpy terminates.

sections.title: --legacy-paste
sections.body:
Inject computer clipboard text as a sequence of key events on Ctrl+v (like MOD+Shift+v).

This is a workaround for some devices not behaving as expected when setting the device clipboard programmatically.

sections.title: --list-apps
sections.body: List Android apps installed on the device.

sections.title: --list-camera-sizes
sections.body: List the valid camera capture sizes.

sections.title: --list-cameras
sections.body: List cameras available on the device.

sections.title: --list-encoders
sections.body: List video and audio encoders available on the device.

sections.title: --list-displays
sections.body:
List displays available on the device.

-m, --max-size  value
Limit both the width and height of the video to value. The other dimension is computed so that the device aspect-ratio is preserved.

Default is 0 (unlimited).

-M
Same as --mouse=uhid, or --mouse=aoa if --otg is set.

sections.title: --max-fps  value
sections.body: Limit the framerate of screen capture (officially supported since Android 10, but may work on earlier versions).

sections.title: --mouse  mode
sections.body:
Select how to send mouse inputs to the device.

Possible values are disabled, sdk, uhid and aoa:

 - disabled does not send mouse inputs to the device.
 - sdk uses the Android system API to deliver mouse events to applications.
 - uhid simulates a physical HID mouse using the Linux HID kernel module on the device.
 - aoa simulates a physical mouse using the AOAv2 protocol. It may only work over USB.

In uhid and aoa modes, the computer mouse is captured to control the device directly (relative mouse mode).

LAlt, LSuper or RSuper toggle the capture mode, to give control of the mouse back to the computer.

Also see --keyboard and --gamepad.

sections.title: --mouse-bind  xxxx[:xxxx]
sections.body:
Configure bindings of secondary clicks.

The argument must be one or two sequences (separated by ':') of exactly 4 characters, one for each secondary click (in order: right click, middle click, 4th click, 5th click).

The first sequence defines the primary bindings, used when a mouse button is pressed alone. The second sequence defines the secondary bindings, used when a mouse button is pressed while the Shift key is held.

If the second sequence of bindings is omitted, then it is the same as the first one.

Each character must be one of the following:

 - '+': forward the click to the device
 - '-': ignore the click
 - 'b': trigger shortcut BACK (or turn screen on if off)
 - 'h': trigger shortcut HOME
 - 's': trigger shortcut APP_SWITCH
 - 'n': trigger shortcut expand notification panel

Default is 'bhsn:++++' for SDK mouse, and '++++:bhsn' for AOA and UHID.


-n, --no-control
Disable device control (mirror the device in read-only).

-N, --no-playback
Disable video and audio playback on the computer (equivalent to --no-video-playback --no-audio-playback).

sections.title: --new-display[=[widthxheight][/dpi]]
sections.body:
Create a new display with the specified resolution and density. If not provided, they default to the main display dimensions and DPI.

Examples:

    --new-display=1920x1080
    --new-display=1920x1080/420
    --new-display         # main display size and density
    --new-display=/240    # main display size and 240 dpi

sections.title: --no-audio
sections.body: Disable audio forwarding.

sections.title: --no-audio-playback
sections.body: Disable audio playback on the computer.

sections.title: --no-cleanup
sections.body:
By default, scrcpy removes the server binary from the device and restores the device state (show touches, stay awake and power mode) on exit.

This option disables this cleanup.

sections.title: --no-clipboard-autosync
sections.body:
By default, scrcpy automatically synchronizes the computer clipboard to the device clipboard before injecting Ctrl+v, and the device clipboard to the computer clipboard whenever it changes.

This option disables this automatic synchronization.

sections.title: --no-downsize-on-error
sections.body:
By default, on MediaCodec error, scrcpy automatically tries again with a lower definition.

This option disables this behavior.

sections.title: --no-key-repeat
sections.body: Do not forward repeated key events when a key is held down.

sections.title: --no-mipmaps
sections.body: If the renderer is OpenGL 3.0+ or OpenGL ES 2.0+, then mipmaps are automatically generated to improve downscaling quality. This option disables the generation of mipmaps.

sections.title: --no-mouse-hover
sections.body: Do not forward mouse hover (mouse motion without any clicks) events.

sections.title: --no-power-on
sections.body: Do not power on the device on start.

sections.title: --no-vd-destroy-content
sections.body:
Disable virtual display destroy content on removal flag.

With this option, when the virtual display is closed, the running apps are moved to the main display rather than being destroyed.

sections.title: --no-vd-system-decorations
sections.body: Disable virtual display system decorations flag.

sections.title: --no-video
sections.body: Disable video forwarding.

sections.title: --no-video-playback
sections.body: Disable video playback on the computer.

sections.title: --no-window
sections.body: Disable scrcpy window. Implies --no-video-playback.

sections.title: --orientation  value
sections.body: Same as --display-orientation=value --record-orientation=value.

sections.title: --otg
sections.body:
Run in OTG mode: simulate physical keyboard and mouse, as if the computer keyboard and mouse were plugged directly to the device via an OTG cable.

In this mode, adb (USB debugging) is not necessary, and mirroring is disabled.

LAlt, LSuper or RSuper toggle the mouse capture mode, to give control of the mouse back to the computer.

If any of --hid-keyboard or --hid-mouse is set, only enable keyboard or mouse respectively, otherwise enable both.

It may only work over USB.

See --keyboard, --mouse and --gamepad.

-p, --port  port[:port]
Set the TCP port (range) used by the client to listen.

Default is 27183:27199.

sections.title: --pause-on-exit[=mode]
sections.body:
Configure pause on exit. Possible values are true (always pause on exit), false (never pause on exit) and if-error (pause only if an error occurred).

This is useful to prevent the terminal window from automatically closing, so that error messages can be read.

Default is false.

Passing the option without argument is equivalent to passing true.

sections.title: --power-off-on-close
sections.body: Turn the device screen off when closing scrcpy.

sections.title: --prefer-text
sections.body:
Inject alpha characters and space as text events instead of key events.

This avoids issues when combining multiple keys to enter special characters,
but breaks the expected behavior of alpha keys in games (typically WASD).

sections.title: --print-fps
sections.body: Start FPS counter, to print framerate logs to the console. It can be started or stopped at any time with MOD+i.

sections.title: --push-target  path
sections.body:
Set the target directory for pushing files to the device by drag & drop. It is passed as-is to adb push.

Default is /sdcard/Download/.

-r, --record  file
Record screen to
file .

The format is determined by the

sections.title: --record-format
sections.body: option if set, or by the file extension.

sections.title: --raw-key-events
sections.body: Inject key events for all input keys, and ignore text events.

sections.title: --record-format  format
sections.body: Force recording format (mp4, mkv, m4a, mka, opus, aac, flac or wav).

sections.title: --record-orientation  value
sections.body:
Set the record orientation.

Possible values are 0, 90, 180 and 270. The number represents the clockwise rotation in degrees.

Default is 0.

sections.title: --render-driver  name
sections.body:
Request SDL to use the given render driver (this is just a hint).

Supported names are currently direct3d, opengl, opengles2, opengles, metal and software.

<https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL_HINT_RENDER_DRIVER>

sections.title: --require-audio
sections.body:
By default, scrcpy mirrors only the video if audio capture fails on the device. This option makes scrcpy fail if audio is enabled but does not work.

-s, --serial  number
The device serial number. Mandatory only if several devices are connected to adb.

-S, --turn-screen-off
Turn the device screen off immediately.

sections.title: --screen-off-timeout  seconds
sections.body: Set the screen off timeout while scrcpy is running (restore the initial value on exit).

sections.title: --shortcut-mod  key[+...]][,...]
sections.body:
Specify the modifiers to use for scrcpy shortcuts. Possible keys are lctrl, rctrl, lalt, ralt, lsuper and rsuper.

Several shortcut modifiers can be specified, separated by ','.

For example, to use either LCtrl or LSuper for scrcpy shortcuts, pass lctrl,lsuper.

Default is lalt,lsuper (left-Alt or left-Super).

sections.title: --start-app  name
sections.body:
Start an Android app, by its exact package name.

Add a '?' prefix to select an app whose name starts with the given name, case-insensitive (retrieving app names on the device may take some time):

    scrcpy --start-app=?firefox

Add a '+' prefix to force-stop before starting the app:

    scrcpy --new-display --start-app=+org.mozilla.firefox

Both prefixes can be used, in that order:

    scrcpy --start-app=+?firefox

-t, --show-touches
Enable show touches on start, restore the initial value on exit.

It only shows physical touches (not clicks from scrcpy).

sections.title: --tcpip[=[+]ip[:port]]
sections.body:
Configure and connect the device over TCP/IP.

If a destination address is provided, then scrcpy connects to this address before starting. The device must listen on the given TCP port (default is 5555).

If no destination address is provided, then scrcpy attempts to find the IP address and adb port of the current device (typically connected over USB), enables TCP/IP mode if necessary, then connects to this address before starting.

Prefix the address with a '+' to force a reconnection.

sections.title: --time-limit  seconds
sections.body: Set the maximum mirroring time, in seconds.

sections.title: --tunnel-host  ip
sections.body:
Set the IP address of the adb tunnel to reach the scrcpy server. This option automatically enables --force-adb-forward.

Default is localhost.

sections.title: --tunnel-port  port
sections.body:
Set the TCP port of the adb tunnel to reach the scrcpy server. This option automatically enables --force-adb-forward.

Default is 0 (not forced): the local port used for establishing the tunnel will be used.

-v, --version
Print the version of scrcpy.

-V, --verbosity  value
Set the log level (verbose, debug, info, warn or error).

Default is info for release builds, debug for debug builds.

sections.title: --v4l2-sink  /dev/videoN
sections.body: Output to v4l2loopback device.

sections.title: --v4l2-buffer  ms
sections.body:
Add a buffering delay (in milliseconds) before pushing frames. This increases latency to compensate for jitter.

This option is similar to --video-buffer, but specific to V4L2 sink.

Default is 0 (no buffering).

sections.title: --video-buffer  ms
sections.body:
Add a buffering delay (in milliseconds) before displaying video frames.

This increases latency to compensate for jitter.

Default is 0 (no buffering).

sections.title: --video-codec  name
sections.body:
Select a video codec (h264, h265 or av1).

Default is h264.

sections.title: --video-codec-options  key[:type]=value[,...]
sections.body:
Set a list of comma-separated key:type=value options for the device video encoder.

The possible values for 'type' are 'int' (default), 'long', 'float' and 'string'.

The list of possible codec options is available in the Android documentation:

<https://d.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaFormat>

sections.title: --video-encoder  name
sections.body:
Use a specific MediaCodec video encoder (depending on the codec provided by --video-codec).

The available encoders can be listed by --list-encoders.

sections.title: --video-source  source
sections.body:
Select the video source (display or camera).

Camera mirroring requires Android 12+.

Default is display.

-w, --stay-awake
Keep the device on while scrcpy is running, when the device is plugged in.

sections.title: --window-borderless
sections.body: Disable window decorations (display borderless window).

sections.title: --window-title  text
sections.body: Set a custom window title.

sections.title: --window-x  value
sections.body:
Set the initial window horizontal position.

Default is auto.

sections.title: --window-y  value
sections.body:
Set the initial window vertical position.

Default is auto.

sections.title: --window-width  value
sections.body:
Set the initial window width.

Default is 0 (automatic).

sections.title: --window-height  value
sections.body:
Set the initial window height.

Default is 0 (automatic).

sections.title: EXIT STATUS
sections.body:
scrcpy
will exit with code 0 on normal program termination. If an initial
connection cannot be established, the exit code 1 will be returned. If the
device disconnects while a session is active, exit code 2 will be returned.

sections.title: SHORTCUTS
sections.body:
In the following list, MOD is the shortcut modifier. By default, it's (left)
Alt or (left) Super, but it can be configured by --shortcut-mod (see above).

MOD+f
Switch fullscreen mode

MOD+Left
Rotate display left

MOD+Right
Rotate display right

MOD+Shift+Left, MOD+Shift+Right
Flip display horizontally

MOD+Shift+Up, MOD+Shift+Down
Flip display vertically

MOD+z
Pause or re-pause display

MOD+Shift+z
Unpause display

MOD+Shift+r
Reset video capture/encoding

MOD+g
Resize window to 1:1 (pixel-perfect)

MOD+w, Double-click on black borders
Resize window to remove black borders

MOD+h, Home, Middle-click
Click on HOME

MOD+b, MOD+Backspace, Right-click (when screen is on)
Click on BACK

MOD+s
Click on APP_SWITCH

MOD+m
Click on MENU

MOD+Up
Click on VOLUME_UP

MOD+Down
Click on VOLUME_DOWN

MOD+p
Click on POWER (turn screen on/off)

Right-click (when screen is off)
Turn screen on

MOD+o
Turn device screen off (keep mirroring)

MOD+Shift+o
Turn device screen on

MOD+r
Rotate device screen

MOD+n
Expand notification panel

MOD+Shift+n
Collapse notification panel

Mod+c
Copy to clipboard (inject COPY keycode, Android >= 7 only)

Mod+x
Cut to clipboard (inject CUT keycode, Android >= 7 only)

MOD+v
Copy computer clipboard to device, then paste (inject PASTE keycode, Android >= 7 only)

MOD+Shift+v
Inject computer clipboard text as a sequence of key events

MOD+k
Open keyboard settings on the device (for HID keyboard only)

MOD+i
Enable/disable FPS counter (print frames/second in logs)

Ctrl+click-and-move
Pinch-to-zoom and rotate from the center of the screen

Shift+click-and-move
Tilt vertically (slide with 2 fingers)

Ctrl+Shift+click-and-move
Tilt horizontally (slide with 2 fingers)

Drag & drop APK file
Install APK from computer

Drag & drop non-APK file
Push file to device (see --push-target)



Environment variables

sections.title: ADB
sections.body: Path to adb.

sections.title: ANDROID_SERIAL
sections.body: Device serial to use if no selector (-s, -d, -e or --tcpip=addr) is specified.

sections.title: SCRCPY_ICON_PATH
sections.body: Path to the program icon.

sections.title: SCRCPY_SERVER_PATH
sections.body: Path to the server binary.

sections.title: Compatibility and limits
sections.body:
This Android client implements the scrcpy 3.3.4 protocol; it is not a complete port of the current desktop client. It supports USB host ADB (main mode), TCP ADB and wireless/TLS pairing (optional), video, audio, multitouch, trackpad input, clipboard, H264/AAC recording, screenshots, Android controls and shell commands.
It does not implement USB OTG/HID without mirroring, UHID gamepads, V4L2 virtual cameras, Windows/Linux/macOS window options, or flex displays from later versions. Desktop-only options in the reference manual below describe the PC client; they are not enabled features on A. Automatic A → B clipboard monitoring is not implemented; send it explicitly from the menu. An already started session is kept when the app goes into the background. New connections and automatic retries only start in the foreground.
Video, audio, camera and advanced codec support depend on Android and hardware. Protected app surfaces may appear black, as in scrcpy. An Android update may require a newer server and corresponding protocol changes.
